tldr: MedAgentGym is a scalable interactive training environment with 72,413 code-centric biomedical reasoning tasks across 129 categories from 12 real-world scenarios, enabling LLM agents to be fine-tuned via RL to match proprietary models like gpt-4o.
contributions: A comprehensive benchmark of 72,413 biomedical coding task instances across 129 categories grounded in 12 real-world biomedical scenarios
An executable sandbox training infrastructure using Docker containers with multi-threaded trajectory sampling, interactive feedback, and verifiable ground truth
Extensive benchmarking of 29 LLMs revealing performance gaps between commercial and open-source models in biomedical data science
Med-Copilot, a fine-tuned coding agent achieving competitive performance with gpt-4o via offline and online reinforcement learning
methods: MedAgentGym was constructed by integrating 12 real-world biomedical datasets (e.g., MIMIC-III, eICU, BioCoder, EHRSQL) into a unified benchmark of 72,413 task instances across 129 categories, each encapsulated in isolated Docker environments with pre-installed biomedical dependencies. Interactive feedback mechanisms parse LLM output into structured JSON and translate error messages into natural language for improved debugging. Efficient trajectory collection was enabled via multi-threaded rollouts using Ray and Joblib backends, generating 2,137 successful trajectories (avg. 9.25 turns), 1,646 offline preference pairs, and 2,939 online preference pairs from gpt-4.1-mini. Med-Copilot was trained using a two-stage fine-tuning framework: SFT warm-up followed by offline DPO or online RL (PPO/GRPO).
results: Benchmarking of 29 LLMs revealed substantial performance disparities between commercial and open-source models. Base Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct scored 16.89% average success rate, which improved to 53.87% (+36.98) with SFT, 59.90% (+43.02) with DPO, and 62.17% (+45.28) with GRPO. Base Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct scored 20.12%, improving to 69.56% (+49.44) with GRPO. Med-Copilot-7B achieved performance comparable to gpt-4o on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution tasks across 4,203 tasks from 4 external datasets.
limitations: Significant performance gap between commercial API-based LLMs and open-source LLMs in biomedical coding
Both specialized coding LLMs and medical domain-specific LLMs deliver suboptimal performance, indicating coding-based biomedical reasoning is not adequately captured by either specialization alone
LLMs perform notably worse on open-ended tasks (data analysis, ML prediction) compared to structured tasks (database queries, medical calculations)
Only four out-of-distribution datasets were used for external evaluation, limiting generalization assessment
